title: Getting started with Capstone
answer: Open My Dashboard and choose Start here. The onboarding area organizes the required Orientation, Intake, Projects, and Your team steps and shows whether each one is complete.
content: The Start here area contains Orientation, Intake, Projects, and Your team. Students can review completed answers from this section.

title: Scrum meeting-minutes templates
answer: Open My Dashboard, then Resources. The portal provides separate Word templates for Sprint Planning, Backlog Grooming, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective, plus a guide explaining how to use them.
content: Use one meeting-minutes template per Scrum ceremony. The templates keep the labels that the portal reads so sprint boards, user stories, and standup hours can appear correctly.

title: Sprint Planning template
answer: Use the Sprint Planning minutes template at the start of each sprint to document the goal, team capacity, and committed backlog. Every teammate should submit the same completed file to the related Canvas assignment.
content: Sprint Planning is completed at the start of each sprint and captures goals, capacity, and committed backlog.

title: Daily Scrum template
answer: Use the Daily Scrum minutes template for each standup. Record what each member completed, what they will do next, and any blockers, using the template’s existing labels.
content: Daily Scrum minutes record yesterday, today, and blockers for each member. The exact template labels help the portal read standup hours.

title: Sprint Review and Retrospective
answer: Use Sprint Review minutes to document what shipped, feedback, and acceptance. Use Sprint Retrospective minutes to record what went well, what should improve, and the team’s action items.
content: Sprint Review covers the demo, delivered work, feedback, and acceptance. Sprint Retrospective covers went well, improve, and action items.

title: Showcase preparation checklist
answer: Before the showcase, proofread the poster and slides, export backups to PDF, record a backup demo, test camera/mic/screen sharing, rehearse a 3–5 minute pitch, assign speaking parts, and prepare for judge questions.
content: The public Student Resources page includes before, during, and after showcase checklists. During the presentation, join early, share deliberately, lead with the problem and solution, show the demo, and invite questions.

title: Poster, slides, and demo materials
answer: Most teams prepare a project poster in PDF format, a short slide deck, and either a demo video or live walkthrough. For a virtual showcase, use large readable type, high-contrast visuals, and a tested demo recording as backup.
content: Presentation materials include a poster, short slide deck, and demo video or live walkthrough. The Resources page links to current templates and video guidelines.

title: Choosing the correct FIU logo
answer: Use the reverse gold-and-white lockup on dark or navy backgrounds and the full-color lockup on white or light documents. Use only one lockup, keep clear space around it, and never recolor, crop, stretch, redraw, or add effects.
content: The Brand & Templates area provides official horizontal and stacked logos in SVG, PNG, and PDF formats, including full-color, reverse, white, blue, and black versions.
intents: which fiu logo should i use

title: Official colors and typography
answer: The primary colors are FIU Blue #081E3F and FIU Gold #D1A644. Gold should not be used as body text on white. Use Proxima Nova when available; Arial is the accepted substitute in Word and PowerPoint.
content: Bright Gold #FFCC00 is for small accents. Cyan #00B7D5 is for data or informational accents on navy and should not be used as text on white.

title: Capstone tutorials
answer: The Tutorials page contains short videos for students, sponsors, judges, and alumni. Student topics include a workspace tour, setting up the team Zoom room, and Capstone 1 showcase-day guidance.
content: The Capstone tutorial collection covers standups, sprint boards, minutes, showcase preparation, sponsorship, judging, and alumni sign-in.

title: Project gallery and archive
answer: Use the Projects page to browse the public archive of Capstone work. Projects can be explored by term and discipline, including Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Data Science & AI.
content: The public project gallery contains student Capstone project summaries and an archive extending across past terms.

title: Canvas assignments
answer: Use the Capstone dashboard for portal guidance and resources, but open Canvas for the official weekly assignment and its submission requirements. The dashboard includes an Open Canvas link when an assignment is referenced.
content: The dashboard directs students to Canvas for the current Capstone assignment. This assistant does not read Canvas course data.

title: Grades and private student information
answer: This assistant cannot read or interpret grades, private messages, team contacts, or directory profiles. Sign in to My Dashboard for information that is specific to your account, and contact the instructor if you need help interpreting it.
content: Public showcase pages display projects rather than private student data. Talent and contact details are gated behind verified accounts and student consent.

title: Requesting more help
answer: If the website does not answer your question, use the support-request option in this prototype. Describe what is wrong and what would help. The demo creates a local ticket; it does not email the professor.
content: The Capstone site directs presentation questions to the program contact. The production version will require an owner-approved notification workflow.

title: Proposing or sponsoring a project
answer: Organizations can engage with Capstone by proposing a real problem, mentoring a student team, sponsoring a project, or participating in the showcase. Start on the Engage page for the appropriate path.
content: The Capstone program provides separate engagement paths for mentors, project sponsors, and showcase participants.

title: Becoming a showcase judge
answer: Use the Become a Judge page to join the showcase judging community. The public Tutorials page also includes a short getting-started video for judges.
content: Judges evaluate final presentations, meet students, and can use the published evaluation guidance and tutorial materials.
